moved_refunds.text:
Moved to HalalGoes Admin — Refunds: https://claude.ai/artifact/NDbFfhcv4MwRgwjmFtpxrx

Sections moved there:
• Refunds — failed refunds first, then look up one order
• Refund form — scope, reason, evidence, confirm
• Refund results — 201, 202, 409 and provider failure

The Refunds page board stays here too, because the order workspace imports it.

s_actions.text:
Cancel is live at launch with an optional case id (owner decision), before and after the restaurant accepts; support agents cancel only before acceptance. The contract still requires a case id, so it is marked Needs API. The panel doesn't say who bears the refund: which refund reason a cancel becomes is Needs API, and the result shows the server's split.

Cancel and reveal are in-page panels that take the place of More detail; the order stays visible beside them. Sign in again is the one dialog.

Cancel and refund are rate limited as money actions; a 429 says nothing was sent and when to try again.

Staff pick from Customer asked to cancel, Restaurant closed, Item unavailable, Cancelled by support, Fraud suspected and Platform error. No rider found is offered only when dispatch is in No rider found. System-only reasons are never offered.

s_alerts.text:
Built only from admin:ops events received while the page is open: admin.alert, admin.dispatch_failure and admin.reconciliation_exception. There is no history or acknowledge, so reloading starts the list again (Needs API).

Rows show only what each event carries. Severity appears only on admin.alert; the other two get a fixed kind badge. A ledger mismatch shows Expected and Recorded exactly as sent, never a difference worked out here. Events name the order by id; the code fills in once getOrderAdmin returns ('Code loading…' until then).

Nav counts come from admin.queue_depth; before the first one the nav shows no number, never 0.

s_cancelled.text:
Result boards are the order the server returns straight after your own cancel; only they carry the one-time 'Cancelled. Refund issued.' banner. Opening a cancelled order from a list shows the plain order, with who cancelled it and why, and no result banner.

System cancels name the rule that fired: restaurant timeout (void), payment expired, restaurant closed at offer time, and no rider after 3 escalations (full refund, restaurant paid, the platform bears it).

A cancelled order never settles, so its refund batch only reverses the charge; provider clearing ends at zero and nothing lands in Platform absorbed except the restaurant's net on a no-rider cancel.

Cancel reason to refund reason is Needs API: the result shows the refund reason the server returned.

s_detail.text:
Three panes, side by side, and the page never scrolls: the list the admin came from (collapsible), the order, and More detail (timeline, map, event log, ledger), each scrolling inside itself. The nav folds to an icon rail while an order is open. The order header holds code, state, the one live Countdown and the actions; the status card's deadline bar is visual only.

While the address is masked, no destination is drawn at all: the masked view still carries the exact destination, and a blur in the browser would not protect it.

Actions follow what the system will do anyway. Preparing and Ready for pickup: the countdown leads, a line says the order cancels and refunds itself, and refund and cancel sit in More actions. Before acceptance the system cancels on its own too (15 minutes to confirm payment, 180 s for the restaurant), so Cancel order sits in More actions as a destructive item, with a line saying so; the case id is optional (owner decision). Delivered, Completed, Disputed and Resolved: Issue refund is a visible button.

The list pane is the list the admin came from: Still running, the open disputes in deadline order, or All orders with its filters; its count is the rows shown. It is one roving tab stop.

Cancel, reveal and the refund panel open in place of More detail, never a dialog; Close or Done brings More detail back. The live map widens More detail over the list. No rider ratings (a V1 feature).

s_detail2.text:
A failed refund holds settlement, but the order keeps its deadline: settlement re-arms with backoff and pages on-call, so Delivered keeps the countdown to the next settlement attempt with 'Held while a refund has failed' beside it. The Orders grid says the same: 'settles, held: a refund failed'. The one entry point is 'Issue a new refund' in the order header, prefilled from the failed one; the banner points to it. A failed row's split reads 'Would have been borne by'.

Ledger entries: capture posts customer charges against provider clearing; settlement splits clearing to restaurant, rider and platform; refunds reverse the charge; provider fees post against platform revenue. Every account, component and batch kind has a label. No tax is charged while HST registration is open, so there are no tax postings; the tax labels stay in the state catalogue legend. Whether payout batches attach to one order is Needs API.

The order pane leads with Refunds on these boards; More detail leads with the ledger where the board is about it. Refund rows show requested and settled times and the provider's message only. Who requested a refund is Needs API.

The ledger banner shows whenever ledger_residual_cents isn't zero on a finished order, from getOrderAdmin. The live admin.reconciliation_exception event only raises it on an open page.

The approval-pending board shows where a request would sit if approval requests were readable on the order.

s_detail3.text:
Three origins of a dispute are drawn: customer after completion or delivery, support mid-delivery with the rider still live, and the restaurant before pickup. The dispute panel holds its own deadline and the refund action, with the warning that a refund doesn't close the dispute and the refunds already on the order.

The refund panel never offers Dispute resolution: that code belongs to resolving the dispute (Needs API). Support agents can refund within their limit, but not goodwill or Before a chargeback.

No package seals at launch (owner decision), so no seal step and no seal-chain board. Whether the automatic resolution refunds, and whether it nets off earlier refunds, is Needs API.

s_disputes.text:
A dispute is an order in the Disputed state: listOrdersAdmin with state=DISPUTED, which returns newest first. The page follows every cursor until has_more is false, then sorts by deadline_at. Until then the header says 'Loading all open disputes: 4 of 6 so far' and makes no sort claim, because an older dispute on a later page can be the most urgent. If a page fails, the list stays newest first and says so. Server sort is Needs API.

The total comes from admin.queue_depth.open_disputes over the socket. The deadline header is plain text, not a sort control.

At each deadline the dispute escalates to senior ops and gets 24 hours more, up to 3 times; after the third it resolves in the customer's favour. Why each order is disputed is one Needs API note above the grid, not a column.

s_map.text:
The live map opens inside the order workspace: More detail widens over the list, the nav stays on the icon rail and the order stays beside it. Its one close control brings More detail back; Reveal address… opens its panel in the same place.

The strip on top holds the deadline (the page's one live timer), the delivery estimate (eta_at on the admin order view) and the leg, from dispatch_state: Assigned or At restaurant = to pickup; Carrying or At customer = to drop-off. A pickup estimate is Needs API: pickup_eta_at reaches only customer, restaurant and rider audiences.

Rider ratings are a V1 feature and aren't shown. A drop reason comes only from dispatch.unassigned while the page is open.

No destination is drawn while the address is masked. The finished message sits outside the map picture, as a status, and in the text equivalent.

Your connection reconnecting, this computer offline and a session that ended are three different banners.

Your connection and the rider's signal are separate problems. A stale pin keeps full opacity with a dashed outline, a Stale badge and 'last known' in its label. Pins are proposed MapPin components: Solar glyph in a token-coloured pin. Rider and destination share forest by owner decision and differ by glyph and label.

s_orders.text:
The grid is drawn on the DataTable component inside a dashed 'LyteNyte' frame: 44px rows, rich cells (Badge, HalalBadge operational, Price, Countdown). Rows are one roving tab stop.

Next deadline: remaining time plus what happens at zero (auto-cancels, escalates, settles). Only Waiting for restaurant (180 s) and Disputed (48 h) get urgency colour; the rest need state_since. Final states show an empty cell with hidden text 'No deadline, final state'.

Items read '2 items: A, B' from item_count and first_item_names and wrap to two lines. A missing halal field shows plain 'No status on file', never a badge.

A refreshed row gets an 'Updated' badge, not the selection tint. The critical board is drawn as it looks under reduced motion: critical colour, no pulse.

Past the deadline, before the server moves the order, the cell reads '0:00, passed 8 s ago' and what is due. Countdown renders nothing after zero, and the page never re-arms a deadline itself.

Placed is a fixed caption, 'newest first': listOrdersAdmin has no sort parameter. Account id filters by account_id and is checked as a UUID before searching.

Support agents see the same grid and filters.

The page never scrolls: filters take one row (Restaurant id and Account id sit behind More filters), and the grid scrolls inside its own region, virtualised. Placed shows the short date; the tooltip carries the full date.

s_reflow.text:
The 200% boards are a 1440 × 900 window at 200% text zoom: 720 × 450 CSS px, drawn at twice the size. The nav folds behind Menu, the order workspace shows one pane at a time (Show: List, Order, More detail), and the Orders filters fold behind a Filters button. The page never scrolls; panes and grids scroll inside themselves.

At 1280 px the list and More detail panes narrow; the grid scrolls sideways inside its region for its last column.
